The image shows soybean leaves with a white to gray powdery coating covering large portions of the leaf surfaces. The powdery patches appear to have coalesced across multiple leaves, affecting both upper and lower portions of the canopy. The coating gives leaves a dusty, pale appearance. No distinct brown lesions, pustules, or necrotic spots are visible — the dominant feature is the diffuse white/gray powdery surface coverage.

This matches Powdery Mildew: "White, powdery coating on leaves that begins as small patches and coalesces to cover entire leaves" and "White to gray powdery patches on leaves that coalesce to cover entire leaf surface."
